body:
This is working somewhat by design. Cloning steps are generally viewed as a mistake, and we try to not introduce any new ones. The amount of internal non-DOM state an element can have is extremely high, and picking out some state to clone causes endless questions of the form "why not also clone X?". In the end we prefer if cloning elements behaves roughly the same as serializing then parsing them, i.e., only clones DOM state like attributes, not internal state like selectedness and dirtiness.

So from this perspective the fact that input elements have cloning steps is unfortunate legacy. Maybe you could argue we should extend it to select/option for consistency, but it's not clear the benefits outweigh the costs. Plus, there might be serious compat issues, which we generally don't want to spend energy investigating with the "goal" of spreading the unfortunate cloning steps concept further.

We can leave this issue open to track adding a note to the spec (perhaps both one to select/option explaining the inconsistency with input, and one to DOM's cloning steps explaining how and why they should be avoided going forward). But I don't think we will change current behavior here.

> Cloning steps are generally viewed as a mistake

Didn't knew that, but I do understand the point of view on the matter. Like you said further into your comment, adding a note in the specs for this could be a step forward in avoiding people opening issues like mine. 

It may even encourage web browsers to add warning in the console when using cloning, linking back to the probably-future note on cloning, as you are saying this is discouraged.

> Maybe you could argue we should extend it to select/option for consistency

I won't lie, I did expected some kind of consistency between, at least, elements being part of forms (or at least, the one being read by FormData). As you said, this could unfortunately unfold to many more issue similar to this one about other html elements.

> but it's not clear the benefits outweigh the costs

It's a very special case, I have to agree on that. I might be one of the rare person encountering the issue, so I won't really push the matter further. Plus, if it causes compatibility issues, I don't think it will _ever_ outweigh the costs
